Apostate Charms

Clambering Horror Mechanism

EX3

Regard, explorer, this roiling, churning sea of viscous black. Cold and dark in its upper reaches, the pressure grows too great for any but the hardiest constructs to survive. Helical forms spin and drift in its depths, collecting samples to ensure the machinegod’s health, refining impurities away and sending life-giving fluids to its citizens far and wide.

Behold, explorer, this foreboding expanse where noxious smoke billows and churns. On detritus-islands lashed together by gravitational eddies, hardy survivors cobble sustenance and shelter out of a Realm’s worth of waste and forgotten things. Now, explorer, peer deeper within, to where — nestled and nurtured in the safety of the machine-god’s body — humanity thrives. Autochthon’s body-realm houses not only cities but entire nations. In great factories, citizens work to keep one another fed and safe, and maintain the sleeping Primordial’s industrial organs both as an act of worship and one of necessity. Conduits run beneath the streets, thrumming with Essence. The constant hum of machinery is a lullaby to children in crèche-dormitories, an everpresent reminder of the Great Maker’s love; they’ll live their entire lives cradled within his body. Not far away, vents hiss and automatons dodge the steam discharged as they bustle to deliver messages to awaiting plutarchs.

In riotous gardens, sinuous cable-vines adorned with amethyst blossoms climb precisely crafted terraces. Music fills the air when the Luminors adjust the lamps of an evening: Workers sing hymns to the Great Maker as they carry out their duties, and clockwork mockingbirds call. In vat complexes, attendants carry out one of the most sacred of all duties: shaping blessed clay and magical materials to form a new Alchemical.

The Eight Nations of the Octet drift through the Maker’s body, ever in motion. 30 years into the latest convergence, the nations huddle together. Pneumatic tubes hurtle through the dark between cities, carrying humans and Alchemicals alike on pilgrimage to Thutot, the first metropolis; on repair missions to the Great Maker’s industrial organs; deployed to protect cities from gremlins; or on diplomatic missions that might prevent or spark a war.

Atop one such tube, Foremost Fist of Righteousness dodged an Apostate’s blow. Perhaps she ought to have been frightened. They were, after all, traveling at immense speed, hugging the boundary of the Endless Smoke with little to catch them should they fall. Somewhere far below, the hulk of a massive, abandoned harvester drifted. Fist caught occasional glimpses of light flashing off jagged metal where an explosion had torn apart its hull. Or perhaps if she avoided that, an immense machine spirit might be gliding along at a fortuitous trajectory. Fist couldn’t rule out the likeliest possibility: They’d simply fall for hours or days, until they plunged into the Endless Smoke and washed ashore on some scavenger’s island.

Instead of frightened, she was exhilarated. The air rushing past reminded her of the Populat’s cheers at home in Claslat. Now and then, lights glinted off their forms as the tube passed through bits of infrastructure: flashes of gold where it caught Fist’s strikes, glimmers of almost liquid silver as her opponent lashed out with a kick from a pistondriven leg. She almost had to admire his design: four legs to her two, all sleek and spindly. But there wasn’t time for appreciation. Again, she thought of Claslat’s people. They were who she fought for. She protected them against threats like this skittering Apostate.

“What were you going to do?” she asked as she ducked another kick. She cocked her arm back with a series of ratcheting clicks and circled slowly, luring him closer. “Derail this tram? You’d die with it.”

“All things should die,” he said. “Even the Maker. Especially the Maker.” Cold horror washed through Fist at the conviction in his voice. The lights flashed on him one more time, illuminating his face: handsome, maybe, if his eyes weren’t alight at the idea of murder.

“You first,” she whispered, and swung her Piston-Driven Megaton Hammer. The blow hit him square in the chest. The Apostate gasped as brass bones crunched. His legs scrabbled for purchase on the tram’s sleek steel, but it was too late. He pitched out over the side, into the emptiness. Fist peered over the edge. Her anima glowed around her now, illuminating him for a while before the darkness engulfed him and the tram carried her away.

The subminister had said there was something lurking in these tunnels. Swiftly Fading Echo had heard rumors about it for weeks now, embedded in the machine spirits’ fretful buzzing.

Other unfortunate parties had gone looking for it. They’d disappeared into the Reaches and not been heard from since. Echo’s other duties had kept them from looking into it until only a few days ago, when the subminister’s assignment had reached them, ordering Echo to make this a priority.

They’d taken little with them: their skycutter, some glow-tubes, a journal for their observations. They’d pondered taking provisions in case they came across any of the missing, but by then it was surely too late.

So into the tunnels they went, into the dark, to learn what had the spirits so afraid. Now they weren’t sure how long they’d been running — hours, surely, though here in the dark it might have been minutes or days. They’d come upon the monster without realizing that was what it was. The biomechanical abomination was the size of a

factory, its body covered in plates of the same dull gray metal of the tunnels Echo was exploring. Its segmented body stretched on into the cavern, with entirely too many insectoid legs protruding from all sides. Diamond-tipped feet dug into the metal walls, giving the horror purchase. From within its mass came the sound of grinding gears and shearing metal. Echo’s nostrils burned with the scent of molten iron. A darkened circular pane sat near the top of its head... darkened, that was, until Echo crossed some invisible line.

The aperture irised open and an angry red light flared to life. A horizontal seam at about Echo’s hip-level split the creature’s head, and that awful grinding sound grew louder. The creature roared.

It chased them through the tunnels, skitter-lumbering close behind the fleeing Alchemical. Its stride shook rusted plates loose. Echo dodged the falling debris and turned to hurl their skycutter toward the gremlin’s glowing red eye. The weapon made a searing arc through the air. It struck true. The creature roared again. Far ahead, they saw the faint light that was the place where they’d entered the tunnel. It narrowed between here and there, too small — they hoped — for the gremlin to get through. If they made it, they could make it to nearby Claslat and warn the circle of Champions they knew operated out of one of its outlying cities. They had to make it. They would make it. Duty became a prayer, and Echo put on a burst of speed.

Faultless Conciliator had been quiet for so long, the people around them had resumed arguing. To Conciliator’s left were a line of regulators, clad in robes of office made from finely woven fabric. To the Jade Caste’s right were a somber group of Populate protesters, equally lined up but nowhere near so refined in appearance. They wore mass-produced work clothes, many of them oft-mended and thin from age. All of them seemed to have forgotten Conciliator there in between them, bent over the body of the murdered man.

“You killed him,” said one of the workers. His gesture swept across the gathered regulators, implicating them all in the crime. “Probably on Autocrat Lehar’s orders, to keep us scared, keep us from speaking out about anything.” His peers murmured their agreement, but nervousness tinged their tone. He was treading on perilous ground with such a declaration. Still, their line held.

A regulator scoffed. “Or perhaps you killed one of your own. Maybe they disagreed with you and you needed to cow the rest into line.”

Conciliator let it go on for a moment. While they lobbed accusations back and forth, the Champion contemplated the murdered man’s unseeing gaze. Would no one think of the dead?

“Will no one think of the dead?” they asked, aloud this time. They lifted the man’s body gently in their arms as they said it, and rose to their full height. Conciliator towered over humans. Usually they hunched a little to set others at ease, especially children. But now they stood tall, looking down at a crowd shocked into silence. Someone was dead, and the people were frightened. They deserved answers. But first, dignity. “We’ll bring him to the Harvesters,” they said, “and then we’ll sit down and talk.” No one argued as they fell into step behind Conciliator and the dead man. The peace wouldn’t last long, but it would do for now.

The mood in the room was as somber as it ever got, and Aesthetics of Civic Perfection had attended many meetings after devastating losses and times of great scarcity. Here, they faced scarcity again, only this was nothing a different problem than thin supplies of nutrient slurry or a dried-up supply of filaments. The grim-faced Militat strategists bent their heads together and whispered, flipping pages in thick ledgers and murmuring to one another.

He didn’t need to crane his neck or produce the little lenses that helped him see things at a distance to know what was in the ledgers. He’d read the accounts already. Souls, an increasing number of them blank of reincarnation, more of them born every year. The Militat was already feeling the effects of the crisis; such souls were unsuitable for assignment to its ranks. Today, it was a recruitment problem. In a few years’ time, it would leave armies scrambling for defenders.

Aesthetics resisted the urge to trace the whorls of starmetal on the back of his hand. The motion brought him calm when he was alone, but in this place, with everyone already on edge, he didn’t want it mistaken for a sign of boredom or impatience. Instead, he held himself still and serene: if he projected calmness and surety, they’d follow suit. He gave the murmurs a little more time to die down, waiting until those nearest to him subsided into silence.

His contacts in the Tripartite — both Estasia’s and those whose embassies he’d visited — had also expressed growing concern. With fewer souls eligible for assignment in their castes, the branches worried that their already spread-thin numbers would continue to decline. Such a lack of strong leadership would lead to civil unrest. And who, then, was best positioned to guide the Octet toward a solution? Who better than the Militat? Aesthetics stood. When all eyes were on him, he began to speak. “We need to look beyond just Estasia,” he said. “This crisis threatens not only our nation, but all of Autochthonia.”

Someone brought Thousand Dooms Sentinel a drink, and she lifted it to them in praise before taking a sip. She passed the cup to her right, where a young woman took it from

her gloved hand. When she sat among mortals, she often ate and drank with them, even though she didn’t need the sustenance. Food was community, after all, and sharing a taste even if she passed the rest on let her feel that connection. Besides, it was best to tell a story while everyone’s bellies were full. “So there I was,” she said, picking up where she’d left off, “on a narrow bridge with live wires running along either side. I knew I’d have to short them out, or else the man I was tailing might spot me if lightning arced at the wrong moment. The only way to do it was to grab the wires. So I braced myself for the shock...”

They gasped and exclaimed as she described following the voidbringer’s contact through the city. She did some embellishing here, omitted a boring detail there, always in service to the story. Her companions’ engagement warmed her, but deep down, worry gnawed at her like a rat at a container of slurry. The tale didn’t end with her catching the cult or thwarting one of its plots. She hoped that would be how it would end, and that she’d be able to tell the story soon, but time was slipping by and the cult grew bolder by the day. How long until they tried plunging a district into darkness, like her investigations suggested they would?

Tonight, though, she needed rest and laughter while her contacts sought out more information. She signaled for more wine and dove back into her tale.

Divine Axiom Demonstrated sat in the courtyard, watching the workers drill. She needed them all ready should gremlins attack or some other nation launch a raid. Jarish’s people did so much with so little, and many days, even as she dropped into an exhausted rest, she felt like she hadn’t done enough.

“Great Maker, help me be enough,” she prayed. She was Jarish’s Champion, built to be its peoples’ protector. Someday, she hoped, she’d become a metropolis, able to shield her charges within her own sturdy walls. Right now, though, she often felt so small. She closed her eyes and imagined crystal lattices, forming, joining, expanding in a burst of colors in her mind. The exercise centered her. It was orderly, neat, dependable, and best of all predictable when she felt so much was outside her own control. Sometimes, as she workedå her way through pleasing structures — of bismuth, quartz, diamond, cobalt, and more — insights and solutions came to her. She looked now for what things she might be missing, what actions she might take to make herself and the people just a little more ready to face whatever may come.

A worker stumbled, drawing Axiom from her reverie. The person beside him caught him and steadied him.

Axiom rose gracefully to her feet. She still felt unsettled; no answers had come. But she had no time to dwell on it. There was much to be done.

# Introduction

“You are not obligated to complete the work, but neither are you free to desist from it.” — Pirkei Avot

There is a world beyond Creation, a world alive with the endless motion of titanic machinery. This is Autochthonia, the Realm of Brass and Shadows, the world that is the living body of the Machine God. No green thing has ever grown here; no sun’s light has ever touched its vast metal expanse. It is haunted by alien machine gods and stalked by monstrous nightmares of flesh and steel. Survival here is all but impossible — and yet, the Eight Nations still stand. The people of Autochthonia live within the body of their god, toiling to maintain the Great Maker’s industrial organs and world-machinery. It is a harsh existence, ever on the precipice of disaster. It is only by the incalculable effort of millions and the divine power of the Alchemical Exalted that the people of Autochthonia thrive.

The Alchemical Exalted are the Chosen of the Machine God, biomechanical demigods forged from divine metal and heroic souls. They do not rule the Eight Nations, but serve as Champions of the people, a sacred duty greater than any ambition. The eldest Alchemicals transcend their human forms to become metropoli, living cities that offer the Eight Nations a stronghold against Autochthonia’s perils.

The Realm of Brass and Shadows is unforgiving, and the Eight Nations find themselves faced with many challenges: cataclysmic upheavals of Autochthon’s world-machinery, incursions of gruesome techno-organic gremlins, and the ever-present threat to their livelihoods. All the while, the slumbering Autochthon grows ever sicker, his corrupting Blight metastasizing throughout his worldbody. Despair not. There is work to be done.

## This Book at a Glance

Chapter One: The Alchemical Exalted introduces the Chosen of the Great Maker, the machine heroes

forged to stand against the enemies of the gods and the divine Champions of Autochthonia’s Eight Nations. Chapter Two: Autochthonia explores the Realm of Brass and Shadows, the vast realm of world-machinery within the Great Maker’s body the Eight Nations call home.

Chapter Three: Character Creation provides rules for creating Alchemical player characters. Chapter Four: Traits details the unique traits used by Alchemicals, including their Castes and the cold, inhuman Clarity of their Great Curse. Chapter Five: Charms provides an extensive panoply of Alchemical Charms, along with rules for the Rite of Reconfiguration that lets Champions install and remove new Charms.

Chapter Six: Martial Arts and Sorcery contains new martial arts styles that are prominently practiced in Autochthonia, like Thousand Wounds Gear style and Crystal Chameleon style, along with sorcerous spells and initiations from the Realm of Brass and Shadows. Chapter Seven: Artifacts provides a variety of Autochthonian technology and artifacts, including signature Alchemical weapons like beamklaves. Chapter Eight: Quick Characters provides traits for Alchemicals, machine spirits, and gremlins, including information and templates that Storytellers can use to create their own machine spirits.

## Lexicon

Alchemical Exalted: The Chosen of Autochthon, artificial humans wrought from clay and metal and catalyzed by a heroic soul.

EX3

### INTRODUCTION

Autochthon: The Great Maker, The Machine God, the King of All Craftsmen, the ancient Autochthon turned on his kin in the Divine Revolution, lending aid to the traitorous gods and creating the Alchemical Exalted. In time, Autochthon departed Creation, taking his faithful with him. The Machine God slumbers now, but the Eight Nations descended from his faithful still dwell within his vast world-body, Autochthonia. Autochthonia: An entire world of industrial machinery and impossible technology that exists within Autochthon’s body. It is the home to the Eight Nations, a world set apart from Creation and the rest of the cosmos. Also known as the Realm of Brass and Shadows. The Blight: A corrupting, techno-organic sickness that festers within the Great Maker, spreading through Autochthonia with disastrous consequences. blight zone: Regions of Autochthonia afflicted by the Blight.

Clarity: The Great Curse of the Alchemical Exalted, a state of increasingly inhuman rationality and utilitarian efficiency. The Alchemicals are aware of Clarity as a phenomenon, though not of its cursed nature. colossus: An Alchemical of great experience and power who has undergone a full-body reconstruction to become a vast, mechanical titan through the Rite of Reconfiguration.

The Eight Divine Ministers: These powerful machine spirits are the foremost of Autochthon’s souls, akin to the Third Circle demons of the Great Maker’s Yozi kin. The Eight Nations: The foremost states of Autochthonia, with the resources and expertise needed to create new Alchemical Exalted. The Eight Nations are also known collectively as the Octet. The Far Reaches: The strangest and most distant corners of Autochthonia, far from the Eight Nations. The Five Sodalities: Within the Eight Nations, the sodalities are elite trade guilds of artisans, savants, and engineers, entrusted with the secret of creating new Alchemical Exalted. The sodalities are one of the three governing institutions that make up the Tripartite of the Eight Nations.

gremlin: A being corrupted by the Blight. Many of them are warped machine spirits, but the most dangerous are the corrupted Alchemicals known as Apostates.

industrial organ: A great mechanism of Autochthon’s world-body, each unique both in its divine power and critical function.

Machine Saint: An Alchemical who serves one of the Eight Divine Ministers, rather than acting as a Champion for the Eight Nations.

machine spirit: One of Autochthon’s souls. The greatest of these are the Eight Divine Ministers, while the least of them are minor custodians that tend to the myriad mechanisms of Autochthonia.

metropolis: An elder Alchemical that has become a living city, one of the greatest sanctums and strongholds of the Eight Nations. Municipal Charm: An infrastructural-scale Charm installed in a metropolis.

The Olgotary: The Eight Nations’ political class, made up of administrators and bureaucrats who form one of the three governing institutions that make up the Tripartite. The Olgotary consists of plutarchs, who form its bureaucratic, deliberative, and diplomatic branches, the regulators who carry out law enforcement, and the adjudicators who pass judgments on crimes. Each metropolis’ Olgotary is headed by an autocrat, while a grand autocrat oversees them at the national level.

Populat: The working class of the Eight Nations. The Rite of Reconfiguration: The sacred technological ritual by which the Alchemical Exalted can install new Charms and customize their panoply of transhuman power. The Seal of Eight Divinities: A mystical barrier between Autochthonia and the rest of the cosmos, forged by Autochthon himself.

soulgem: A vital component in the creation of the Alchemical Exalted. Citizens of the Eight Nations have one of these jewels implanted in their foreheads shortly after birth. Upon death, members of the Five Sodalities can assess a soul’s potential for catalyzing Exaltation before releasing it from its soulgem to be reborn. subminister: A machine spirit that emanates from one of the Eight Divine Ministers, comparable to a Second Circle demon.

The Theomachracy: The priesthood of Autochthon and the clerical administrative class of the Eight

### Video Games

Nations, making up one of the three governing institutions that make up the Tripartite. Within the Theomachracy’s ranks, lectors preach the Maker’s doctrine and offer spiritual guidance, preceptors enforce orthodoxy and root out heresy, while clerics see to matters of administration, bureaucracy, and doctrine. Each metropolis’ Theomachracy is headed by a celebrant, while a grand celebrant oversees them at the national level.

### Movies

Ghost in the Shell, directed by Mamoru Oshii: Cybernetically-enhanced agents of a morally questionable state, political intrigue, and cyberpunk philosophy make this a keystone for Alchemicals and Autochthonia. The same is true for its 2002 incarnation as an anime series, Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex.

The Tripartite: The governing body within each of the Eight Nations, drawing from the political leadership of the Olgotary, the clerical authority of the Theomachracy, and the expertise of the Five Sodalities. The Alchemical Exalted support the Tripartite, but they don’t belong to it — they are Champions, not leaders.

The Matrix, directed by Lana Wachowski and Lilly Wachowski: The mechanical landscape and terrifying machines of the “real world” offers visual inspiration for Autochthonia and the machine spirits that inhabit it.

tunnel folk: A term used by the Eight Nations to label other human societies that exist in Autochthonia’s Reaches, lacking the protection of Alchemical Champions and metropoli.

Metropolis, directed by Fritz Lang: One of the original inspirations for Autochthonia, Lang’s expressionist masterpiece presents a dystopian vision of futuristic technology and class conflict that laid the foundation for the Eight Nations.

## Suggested Resources

The following media may offer inspiration for players and Storytellers interested in stories centered on the Realm of Brass and Shadows and the Great Maker’s Chosen.

### Fiction

The Golem, by Joachim Neusgroschel: A collection of stories about the famous golem of Prague, the folkloric predecessor of the Alchemical Exalted. Created from clay to guard Jewish communities against antisemitic violence, the golem inspires the Alchemicals’ role as Champions — though they don’t suffer the golem’s traditional propensity for going haywire. I, Robot and the Robots Series, by Isaac Asimov: Asimov’s famous Three Laws of Robotics don’t apply to the free-willed Alchemicals, but these classic short stories offer plenty of inspiration, particularly for Alchemicals engaging with transhuman perspective of Clarity — particularly those robots that approach the “Zeroth Law.”

R.U.R.: Rossum’s Universal Robots, by Karel Čapek: The origin of both the word “robot” and the idea of robots as artificial laborers, R.U.R. is the seed of a vast wave of science fiction that contributed to the aesthetics of Alchemicals and Autochthonia’s mechanical landscape.

Tetsuo: The Iron Man, directed by Shinya Tsukamoto: A foundational work of disturbing techno-organic horror, this film follows an unnamed salaryman’s transformation into a grotesque amalgam of flesh and metal. It’s gruesome inspiration for Autochthonia’s Blight and the biomechanical horrors it creates.

### Television

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, directed by Hiroyuki Imaishi: The Sandevistan and other cybernetic enhancements in this dystopian series make great inspiration for Alchemical Charms, while the dangers of cyberpsychosis touch on the Dissonance of corrupted Alchemical Apostates.

Robot Carnival, by A.P.P.P.: This collection of animated shorts is a celebration of lovingly-detailed machinery, offering a visual feast of Autochthonian aesthetics.

Star Trek: The Next Generation, directed by Gene Roddenberry: Lieutenant Data’s struggle to understand humanity and discover his own isn’t a typical story arc for the Alchemical Exalted, but he’s still the most influential android in fiction, and among the original inspirations for them.

Comics and Manga

BLAME!, by Tsutomu Nihei: This classic cyberpunk manga’s Megastructure is one of the greatest visual inspirations to be found for the world of Autochthonia, while the robotic Safeguard and the cybernetic Silicon Life offer inspiration for machine spirits and gremlins. New Gods, by Jack Kirby: The beautifully illustrated technology of Kirby’s New Gods is wonderful visual inspiration for the wondrous machines and industrial organs found in Autochthonia, as well as the Charms of the Alchemical Exalted.

Video Games

Final Fantasy VII, by Square Enix: A classic RPG of the PlayStation era with numerous tie-ins, Final Fantasy VII’s combination of magic with technology in an industrialized society makes it a great inspiration for the aesthetics of Autochthonian technology. Horizon Series, by Gorilla Games: The machines in these action RPGs serve as great inspiration for machine spirits, including how the machines interact with the ecology of their post-apocalyptic world. The

way the tribes use machine parts and incorporate belief about the machines into their religious practices and machine parts into their gear makes great fodder for Autochthonian traditions, especially among the tunnel folk.

Warframe, by Digital Extremes: The titular Warframes and their customizable upgrades make great inspiration for Alchemical Charms, while the Infestation offers plenty of examples of the horrors created by Autochthonia’s Blight.

Xenoblade Chronicles, by Monolith Soft: This RPG features a clash between biological and mechanical world-titans. The machine-titan Mechonis and its inhabitants serve as great visual inspiration for the machine-world of Autochthonia, its native machine spirits, and the aesthetics of Alchemical Charms.

Music

Metropolis: the Chase Suite and The ArchAndroid, by Janelle Monáe: The dystopian narrative wound through these albums focuses on a messianic android provides both inspiration for Adamant Caste Alchemicals and a great soundtrack for in-person games.

The shape of rubble rose above the ground, beckoning and inviting, like an obstacle course demanding to be conquered. Foremost Fist of Righteousness never backed away from a challenge, but especially not one written so plainly in the scenery. Sure, there were probably more important things to focus on at the moment. She could hear the voice of her Circlemates in her mind, chiding her for making everything and anything into a competition. Such was the talk of unambitious people.

Stern Whip of Industry was, similarly, not motivated by a desire to chase the taste of victory. The massive, staid man directed the workers with an irritating calm. Where was his sense of joy? His verve? His taste for life? Fist had met propaganda posters with more energy. “I bet I can clear more rubble than you can, and I bet I can open the way through faster than you.” She spoke aloud, her low voice echoing off the maintenance tunnel’s walls. “It is not a competition,” he replied in his pleasantly deep voice. “We are here to make sure this area is safe and accessible again.”

Predictable. Foremost Fist stifled a groan. “C’mon, Big Red, don’t you want to have fun with it?” “My designation is Stern Whip of Industry,” he said humorlessly, “and we are here to save lives. It isn’t for fun.”

At this, Foremost Fist placed her bulky width between him and the collapsed tunnel. She squared her shoulders and pumped Essence through her reinforced heart to give her an air of leadership. His attention fell upon her, even though he was annoyed.

“Listen here, Big Red,” she said and made a gesture to silence the protest he started voicing. “It is equally important to enjoy oneself as it is to do the work. There’s no point in being heroes if we aren’t having a good time about it. So, bearing that in mind, I bet I can clear more rubble than you.”

The raw charisma of her words moved the big red lunk to heave a gusty, defeated sigh. She’d take it. “Very well,” he said with what she decided was a hint of a smile. “I shall soundly defeat you in this endeavor if this means you will take the task seriously.”

“I am always taking things seriously,” Fist retorted, but Stern Whip of Industry had already launched into motion.

He moved like an unchained machine as he turned aside hefty chunks of reinforced plastic and steel and pushed away debris with wide sweeps of his massive arms. Stern Whip of Industry pressed the heels of his thick palms together and heaved away dirt and detritus like a shovel in the form of a man. Furious at possibly being outdone, Foremost Fist of Righteousness fired a tether beam from her wrist’s hidden compartments, hooked into a spar of concrete, and sailed past his head. He looked up placidly as she soared by. Fist winked and made a saucy gesture with her free hand. If the other Alchemical reacted, she didn’t see, as she landed several yards away and launched into her own fervent work. She lifted and threw; she dug and delved; she carried rebar and rubble until a pristine path was clear. Sweat gathered around her collar and itched in the joints of her mechanical physique. It glistened on the studs of orichalcum and jade that stuck from her chest, biceps, and thighs. When she glanced back, Stern Whip of Industry leaned on a girder, having done twice the work she’d managed in the same amount of time.

A small, self-satisfied smile played across his otherwise stern and unremarkable face. “I think I win,” he said.

# Chapter One: The Alchemical Exalted

Chapter One

The Alchemical

Exalted

The Alchemical Exalted are the Chosen of Autochthon, the Great Maker. They are human, but they are also machine, wrought from sacred clay and divine metal and animated with the souls of heroes. In Autochthonia, they are Champions of the Eight Nations who dwell within the Machine God. A scarce few remain hidden in Creation, heroes forged to fight the enemies of the gods, but never deployed.

## History

Before the first moment of time, they arose. They created themselves from chaos and nothingness, and ushered in the dawn of reality. Primordial, they named themselves in the crude language of the gods they created, older than the oldest things. At their command, the seas of chaos froze into law. Among their number was Autochthon, the Great Maker, a tinker and a trickster among the titans. In the time before, the Great Maker and his kin roamed the endless possibilities of the Wyld. They fashioned splendors unimaginable and horrors fearsome even to themselves, scattering ephemeral worldlets like stepping stones before them. They warred against the devouring legions of the ancient Fair Folk; consorted with the poisoned flame that was not yet the Scorpion Empire; laid siege to a castle that doesn’t exist, and found themselves defeated. There was the grand folly that was Zen-Mu, and the bitter war that came after. Soon, the Primordials would undertake their greatest work, the making of Creation. Autochthon delighted in it. He hammered out mountains and welkin-glass on his forge, brought life to the Jadeborn and the gigantes, and invented several very useful prime numbers. He worked from beyond the world as the Primordials raised Heaven over Creation, the architect of their impossible spatial geometries. He raised

factory-cathedrals and starspires like sandcastles, shaping and reshaping the world.

But Autochthon was scorned by his kin, who had long mocked him as a sickly, ugly runt. The cruelest of them delighted in tearing down his greatest creations, leaving him to grieve over the ruins. Loath as he was to endure this, the Great Maker could not stand alone against the other Primordials. He could not make them love him or fear him, but he could make himself useful to them. He offered them wonders from his forge, played on their vanity, and learned to make their hatred for him into a tool. Even then, this reprieve was a paltry thing, lasting only as long as he could keep his hateful siblings so distracted.

Estranged from his Primordial kin, Autochthon sympathized with those gods who plotted to overthrow their makers, offering them what succor and counsel he could. When the Celestial Incarnae discovered the secret of Exaltation, it was Autochthon who showed them how such power might be fashioned into a weapon. He crafted his own Exalted alongside them, the first Alchemicals, demonstrating both the power of the Exalted and his dedication to the cause. He forged weapons and armor for the gods and their Chosen and revealed to them great mysteries of artifice, the many secret methods of refining the magical materials to build weapons of war. But Autochthon still feared his Primordial kin, and struggled to keep his labors hidden from them. He created only a scarce few Alchemicals compared to the other gods’ Chosen, and awoke only a few of their number to fight.

The gods waged their terrible war against the Primordials and won, though not before staining Creation with the blood of slain titans. The gods claimed Heaven for themselves, and the Exalted host reigned ascendant over Creation, but Autochthon knew there would be no place for him. He knew that

EX3

## The Creation of an Alchemical

he would forever be a reminder of the Primordials’ cruelty, and that the Exalted would never forget his own treachery against his kin. For a while, he thought he could bear to linger, but in time, this hope gave way to his fears. Thus he took himself beyond Creation, accompanied by his faithful and followers, and sealed the path to those who might attempt to follow. Now the Machine God slumbers, still sickly as he once was. The mortals he brought within him dwell within a world that is his flesh, the ever-shifting engine-realm of Autochthonia. There, they founded the Octet, eight great nations that labor in worship to the Great Maker. Instructed by the Great Maker himself, the Eight Nations hold the secret of creating new Alchemical Exalted. These Alchemicals do not rule, but serve. They are exemplars of national service, inspiring people and aiding the governance of the nations. They are conduits between mortals and the divine, interceding with the machine spirits that inhabit Autochthonia’s reaches. As their power grows, they become the very cities that house their people. The strength and innovation of the Eight Nations and their Champions hold back the creeping Blight, the sickness of their Maker, which threatens all who dwell within him.

The Creation of

an Alchemical

The Alchemicals are a gift from the Great Maker to his people. They are born of matter, motion, and miracle: the precious reagents needed to shape their body and Charms, the exacting skill and sublime artistry required to create them, and the spark of the Great Maker comingling with mortal souls. After months of work, ritual, and sacrifice, Autochthon’s Essence courses through the flesh of his newest Chosen, and the people rejoice in welcoming their fledgling Champion. When a nation commissions the creation of a new Alchemical, the work falls to the five Sodalities, technologist guilds that preserve the secrets of Exaltation handed down by the Great Maker, each safeguarding one part of the process. Work begins with the Surgeons, who shape the Champion’s body from sacred clay and wax. The Harvesters concoct the catalytic vat-broth in which a nascent Alchemical gestates, but it must be heated and tended in precise rites known only to the Conductors. The Scholars craft the Alchemical’s Essence reservoir and the Charms that will imbue the Champion with its divine might. Finally, the Luminors attach the soulgem to the nascent Alchemical, quickening the connection between body and soul. The

Great Maker’s will works through the artisans in that final moment, and the Alchemical awakens…if the soul is worthy.

Kanesh puts his palm to the clay to warm it. His hands are anointed with the sacred unguents, and he is a Surgeon of meticulous skill, but still — the clay must be warm. Today, he shapes the Champion’s face, and gives it his mother’s high cheekbones. Much of his work may be undone when the Alchemical wakes from the broth and the holy clay of their form is Essence-fired into their self-image, but sometimes they keep what they are given. They are children with many parents — the Sodalities, the souls of heroes, the nation, the Maker — and he plays his part in that tender work. Mortal souls are the key to Autochthon’s miracle of Exaltation, requiring a heroic legacy forged over past lifetimes to catalyze a Champion’s Exaltation. Each of the six Alchemical Castes has its own criteria, and the Autochthonians’ understanding of them is imperfect, though guided by millennia of trial and error. The souls they choose must be exceptional to have any hope of attracting the unconscious attention of the Great Maker, and so they keep meticulous records of each soul’s deeds and distinctions. While those souls marked as candidates for Exaltation have usually distinguished themselves over multiple incarnations, some are selected after a single lifetime of truly exceptional heroism. “Have I lived well?” Dargen asks, but no one can hear. The skirmish continues, even as his blood pools from the wound. He will die in these tunnels with gremlin bile on his pike, die for his city and the other warriors of his battalion. The fatal blow hadn’t been meant for him, but he made his flesh a bulwark for…who was it? Jadia? Lyzed? It doesn’t matter. It bites at him that his last thoughts are selfish. Was his sacrifice real, or vainglorious? Who was he to think his death had to mean something? As the light goes out of his eyes, he dreams that when his soul next stirs, it will be in the body of a Champion. If all is successful, the newly Exalted Alchemical emerges from the vats. They are not a resurrection of any past self, but a wholly new entity, greater than the sum of their mortal parts. The Champion understands who and what they are, and has skills and knowledge drawn from memories of their previous incarnations. Many new Alchemicals dream with curiosity about previous lives or feel phantom affections for lost loves; some make lifelong studies of their prior lives.
